literature_notes: All eight ledger lines (L1–L8) describe tags appended to the C-terminus of full-length FGFR1. The computed topology places the C-terminus (residue 822, R) deep in the intracellular domain (IC: 396–822). L1–L6 report 2xMyc knock-in alleles (Fgfr1 Myc and Fgfr1 FCPGMyc) validated in vivo; L7–L8 report an FGFR1-EGFP C-terminal fusion used for subcellular localisation. None of these insertions is on the extracellular face. No ledger line describes a tag at the mature N-terminus (residue 22), in any extracellular loop, or anywhere in the EC domain (22–374). The mature N-terminus (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 21) is extracellular and would in principle accept a prepended tag, but no ledger line grounds such an insertion for FGFR1 or a close ortholog. Zero surface sites qualify.

literature_other_positions.note: 2xMyc tag appended to C-terminus of full-length FGFR1; Fgfr1 Myc/Myc mice viable and fertile, confirming tag does not compromise receptor activity — but the C-terminus (residue 822) is intracellular (IC span 396–822), so this is not a surface tag site.
FGFR1-EGFP C-terminal fusion (R1-GFP) used to study subcellular localisation of full-length FGFR1; C-terminus (residue 822) is intracellular, so this is not a surface tag site.
